title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 2.4 Hadith on Fitness

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Islam wants a believer who is strong enough to worship Allah, help people and stay healthy. In this sub-strand you will read the Hadith on teaching children useful physical skills, learn which games are allowed, and practise the Islamic manners of sport.

## Strand 2.0: Hadith
Sub-strand 2.4: Hadith on Fitness
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) read the selected hadith on physical fitness to promote healthy living
b) assess the importance of physical fitness in the life of a Muslim
c) participate in games and sports while observing Islamic values
d) value the importance of physical fitness as means of being dearer to Allah (S.W.T)

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should one be physically fit?
2. What Islamic rules should a Muslim observe while participating in games and sports activities?

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of teamwork is enhanced through discussing the importance of physical fitness and values derived from participating in games and sports.
• Learning to learn: the skill of sharing learnt knowledge is enhanced as learners discuss the Islamic etiquette to be observed during games and sports activities.
• Citizenship: the skill of social skills is enhanced as learners discuss the Islamic etiquette to be observed during games and sports activities.

## Values
• Respect: acceptance is enhanced as learners respect each other opinion during discussion.
• Responsibility: self-drive is enhanced as learners demonstrate etiquette to be observed during games.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Learner support programmes through participating in games and sports

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: as they participate in various games and sports activities
• Agriculture: by avoiding lifestyle diseases through exercises and promoting good health.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 2.0 Hadith, Sub-strand 2.4 Hadith on Fitness
• Hadith as given in the design: “Teach your children swimming, archery and horse riding.” (Narrated by Muslim)
• Sahih Muslim: a strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak believer; Sahih al-Bukhari: the body has a right over you, and the Prophet raced with Aisha

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: The Hadith on swimming, archery and horse riding

LESSON 1: THE HADITH ON SWIMMING, ARCHERY AND HORSE RIDING
==========================================================

## What you will learn
• Read the selected Hadith on physical fitness.
• Explain why a Muslim cares for the strength of the body.
• Connect fitness with worship and service.

Curriculum outcomes: a) read the selected hadith on physical fitness to promote healthy living; b) assess the importance of physical fitness in the life of a Muslim

## Introduction
A body that never runs, swims or plays soon becomes tired even in swalah. Islam does not ignore the body. A Hadith tells parents to teach children skills that make the body able and brave.

## Notes
### The selected Hadith
The Prophet (S.A.W.) said: “Teach your children swimming, archery and horse riding.” The Grade 4 curriculum gives this Hadith as narrated by Muslim. Swimming teaches a child to be safe and strong in water. Archery trains a steady eye, a calm breath and patience, and it must be done only with a trained adult in a safe place. Horse riding builds balance and courage, and the horse must be treated kindly.

### A believer who is strong
Another Hadith, in Sahih Muslim, says that a strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak believer, while there is good in both. Strength here includes the body and a firm heart. The Prophet (S.A.W.) also taught that the body has a right over you (Bukhari). Sleep, food and movement are part of that right. Fitness is not vanity. It helps a Muslim stand in qiyam, walk to the mosque, work, and help a person who needs to be carried or supported.

### Why fitness matters
- It keeps the body healthy and can prevent some illnesses that come from sitting still all day.
- It gives energy for ibadah and for schoolwork.
- It teaches courage and self-control.
- The three skills in the Hadith are useful, not only entertaining.
- A healthy Muslim can serve parents and neighbours.

Read the selected Hadith aloud and write it in your notebook. Remember that fitness is a means of drawing nearer to Allah when it is used in obedience, not when it leads a person to skip swalah or to show off.

## Key words
• physical fitness — a healthy, strong body gained through regular activity
• archery — the sport of shooting arrows at a target, practised safely with an adult

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A boy says games are a waste of time because a Muslim should only sit and read. How do the two Hadiths answer him?

Working:
1. Children are taught swimming, archery and horse riding.
2. A strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak believer, and there is good in both.
3. The body has a right, so movement is part of the religion when it stays within Islamic rules.

Answer: Islam teaches useful physical skills. Strength that is used well is beloved to Allah, and the body has a right.

## Activity: Read the Hadith and list reasons
You will need: Hadith card, Notebook
1. Read: “Teach your children swimming, archery and horse riding.”
2. In groups, discuss why a Muslim should be physically fit.
3. Write four reasons in your notebook.
4. Share them with the class and listen to other groups.

## Practice
1. State the selected Hadith on physical skills.
2. What does the Hadith in Sahih Muslim say about a strong believer and a weak believer?
3. Give two reasons why physical fitness matters for a Muslim.

## Summary
• The Hadith names swimming, archery and horse riding as skills to teach children.
• A strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak one, and there is good in both.
• The body has a right, so fitness supports worship and service.

### Answers to practice
1. “Teach your children swimming, archery and horse riding.”
2. A strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak believer, and there is good in both.
3. Any two: health, energy for ibadah, courage, serving other people, or following the skills named in the Hadith.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Games that are allowed and the values they teach

LESSON 2: GAMES THAT ARE ALLOWED AND THE VALUES THEY TEACH
==========================================================

## What you will learn
• Name games and sports that are permissible in Islam.
• Explain values gained from taking part, such as fair play and teamwork.
• Identify games that a Muslim should avoid.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the importance of physical fitness in the life of a Muslim; c) participate in games and sports while observing Islamic values

## Introduction
Not every game that a crowd enjoys is suitable for a Muslim. Some games build the body and the character. Others involve gambling, cruelty or missed prayers. This lesson sorts them.

## Notes
### Permissible games and sports
A game is permissible when it is itself halal and it is played within Islamic manners. Examples include:

- Swimming, in a safe place and with a person who can help
- Running and athletics
- Football, netball and similar ball games
- Archery with proper safety and an adult
- Horse riding while treating the horse kindly
- Skipping, traditional races and other school games that do not involve haram

The Prophet (S.A.W.) allowed and took part in lawful physical activity. He raced on foot with his wife Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her). Companions trained in riding and archery. The aim was strength and joy within the limits of Allah.

### Values from sport
Taking part properly teaches teamwork, sharing of equipment, humility in winning, fair play, discipline and leadership. A captain who rotates players is learning justice. A team that passes the ball is learning to share. A loser who congratulates the winner is learning humility.

### What to avoid
Avoid games built on gambling, games that require harming a person or an animal for fun, and games that make you miss swalah on purpose or expose the awrah. If a match is running into Maghrib, the Muslim stops for prayer. Fitness loses its value when it breaks a command of Allah.

## Key words
• permissible — allowed in Islam
• fair play — playing by the rules and not cheating
• halal — lawful

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A team wants to finish a football match even though the adhan for Maghrib has been called, and the losers must pay money to the winners. What is wrong?

Working:
1. Swalah at its time comes before the rest of the match.
2. Paying money because of a win or loss is gambling.
3. They should pause, pray, and play without bets.

Answer: They must stop for Maghrib and they must not gamble. The game itself can continue later without bets.

## Activity: Sort permissible and forbidden games
You will need: Cards naming different games and situations, Two labelled boxes or areas: Allowed and Not allowed
1. In groups, discuss each card: swimming, a football match with a cash bet, archery with a teacher, a race that continues through Asr without praying, horse riding with a tired beaten horse.
2. Place each card under Allowed or Not allowed and give the reason.
3. List the values a fair game can teach: teamwork, sharing, humility, fair play, discipline and leadership.
4. Write the two lists in your notebook.

## Practice
1. Name three sports or skills that are permissible for a Muslim learner.
2. Name four values that fair games can teach.
3. Give two reasons a game would not be allowed.

## Summary
• Swimming, running, ball games, safe archery and kind horse riding can be permissible.
• Good games teach teamwork, sharing, humility, fair play, discipline and leadership.
• Gambling, cruelty and missing swalah take a game outside Islamic limits.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: swimming, running, football, netball, archery with safety, horse riding with kindness to the horse.
2. Any four: teamwork, sharing, humility, fair play, discipline, leadership.
3. Any two: it involves gambling, it harms people or animals for fun, it causes swalah to be missed on purpose, or it exposes the awrah.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Islamic etiquette during games and sports

LESSON 3: ISLAMIC ETIQUETTE DURING GAMES AND SPORTS
===================================================

## What you will learn
• State the Islamic manners to observe while playing.
• Demonstrate modest dress and stopping for swalah.
• Explain how fitness, used well, makes a believer dearer to Allah.

Curriculum outcomes: c) participate in games and sports while observing Islamic values; d) value the importance of physical fitness as means of being dearer to Allah (S.W.T)

## Introduction
The rules of a game tell you how to score. The rules of Islam tell you how to behave while you play. Dress, language, prayer times and fairness all stay in force on the field.

## Notes
### Etiquette to observe
While you take part in games and sports:

- Dress modestly. A boy covers from the navel to the knees. A girl covers her awrah with a decent sports kit that is not see-through. Clothes should let you move safely without displaying what Islam tells you to cover.
- Keep the times of swalah. If a prayer time enters, pause, pray, and return if the game is still lawful.
- Play fair. Do not cheat, trip someone on purpose or argue with insults.
- Use clean language. Foul words do not become halal because a match is exciting.
- Win without pride and lose without anger. Congratulate the others.
- Do not gamble.
- Share the ball, the rope or the space.
- Do not harm the weak, and do not mistreat an animal used in a sport.
- Follow the teacher’s safety rules, especially near water or with archery equipment.

### Valuing fitness
The Hadith of the strong believer shows that strength, joined with faith, is beloved to Allah. A learner values fitness by training regularly, eating and sleeping sensibly, and using strength to obey Allah and help people. Strength used to bully is not the strength that is beloved. When you race fairly, stop for Asr, and help a fallen player, you are making fitness a path towards Allah (S.W.T.).

## Key words
• awrah — the parts of the body that must be covered
• etiquette — the manners observed during an activity

## Worked examples

### Example 1
During a race, a girl is wearing a suitable sports kit. She is about to start the final run when she hears the adhan for Asr. What etiquette should she follow?

Working:
1. Swalah is observed even during sport.
2. She tells her teacher, prays Asr, and keeps her modest dress.
3. She returns to the race only in a way the teacher allows, without cheating.

Answer: She pauses for Asr in modest dress, then continues only as the teacher directs, still playing fairly.

## Activity: Demonstrate match-day manners
You will need: A ball or a skipping rope, A card showing prayer times for today
1. In groups, discuss the etiquette of dress, language, fair play and swalah.
2. Demonstrate a one-minute game. Freeze when the leader calls “Asr” and show how you would leave to pray.
3. Show a modest way of standing and moving for both boys and girls, as your teacher guides.
4. Write five etiquette rules in your notebook and present them.

## Practice
1. State two rules of Islamic dress during games.
2. What should players do when the time for swalah enters during a match?
3. How can physical fitness make a believer dearer to Allah?
4. Name two manners of winning and losing.

## Summary
• Modest dress, fair play, clean speech and swalah remain obligatory during sport.
• Pause a game when prayer time enters.
• Strength is beloved to Allah when it is used in obedience and kindness.

### Answers to practice
1. Cover the awrah. A boy covers from the navel to the knees, and a girl wears a decent kit that covers her awrah and is not see-through.
2. Pause the game and pray, then continue later if the game is still lawful.
3. When strength is joined with faith and used to obey Allah and help people, not to bully or to skip worship. A strong believer is more beloved to Allah than a weak believer, and there is good in both.
4. Win without pride, and lose without anger. Congratulate the other team.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 2.4 HADITH ON FITNESS
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which skills does the selected Hadith tell parents to teach their children?
   A. Gambling, racing for money and wrestling for a prize of money
   B. Swimming, archery and horse riding
   C. Only sitting games
   D. Hunting birds for fun

2. According to Sahih Muslim, who is more beloved to Allah?
   A. A weak believer, and a strong one has no good
   B. A strong believer rather than a weak believer, and there is good in both
   C. Only a person who never plays
   D. The person who wins by cheating

3. The saying that the body has a right over you means…
   A. You may skip every prayer to rest
   B. The body needs proper care, including lawful rest and activity
   C. Sport replaces fasting
   D. Food is not a blessing

4. Which game situation is permissible?
   A. A cash bet on the final score
   B. A football game that stops for Maghrib
   C. A race that mocks the slowest child
   D. Archery aimed at animals for fun

5. Which value is trained when players pass and share equipment?
   A. Envy
   B. Teamwork and sharing
   C. Gambling
   D. Pride

6. A match that continues on purpose through Asr is…
   A. a sunnah
   B. against the etiquette of observing swalah
   C. a pillar of fitness
   D. required by the Hadith

7. How should a boy dress for sport?

8. How should a player behave after losing?
   A. Insult the winners
   B. Refuse to greet them
   C. Lose without anger and congratulate them
   D. Demand money

9. Archery in this Hadith should be practised…
   A. by aiming at classmates
   B. safely, with a trained adult
   C. in the classroom during a test
   D. instead of Fajr

10. When is physical fitness a means of being dearer to Allah?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 2.4 HADITH ON FITNESS
========================================

1. B. Swimming, archery and horse riding
   The Hadith says: teach your children swimming, archery and horse riding.

2. B. A strong believer rather than a weak believer, and there is good in both
   The strong believer is better and more beloved, and there is good in both.

3. B. The body needs proper care, including lawful rest and activity
   This teaching, in Sahih al-Bukhari, balances worship with the rights of the body.

4. B. A football game that stops for Maghrib
   The sport itself is lawful, and stopping for swalah keeps the etiquette.

5. B. Teamwork and sharing
   The design lists teamwork, sharing, humility, fair play, discipline and leadership.

6. B. against the etiquette of observing swalah
   Islamic etiquette includes observing the times of swalah during games.

7. He covers the awrah, from the navel to the knees, in clothing suitable for safe movement.
   Modest dress is part of the etiquette of games.

8. C. Lose without anger and congratulate them
   Humility and fair play apply after the game as well as during it.

9. B. safely, with a trained adult
   It is a skill of focus and calm, done only in a safe setting.

10. When the strong believer uses that strength to obey Allah and help people.
   Strength joined with iman is what the Hadith praises, not bullying or showing off.

3. When strength is joined with faith and used to obey Allah and help people, not to bully or to skip worship. A strong believer is more beloved to Allah than a weak believer, and there is good in both.
4. Win without pride, and lose without anger. Congratulate the other team.

questions.question: Which skills does the selected Hadith tell parents to teach their children?
options: Gambling, racing for money and wrestling for a prize of money
questions.explanation: The Hadith says: teach your children swimming, archery and horse riding.

questions.question: According to Sahih Muslim, who is more beloved to Allah?
options: A weak believer, and a strong one has no good
A strong believer rather than a weak believer, and there is good in both
Only a person who never plays
The person who wins by cheating
questions.explanation: The strong believer is better and more beloved, and there is good in both.

questions.question: The saying that the body has a right over you means…
options: You may skip every prayer to rest
The body needs proper care, including lawful rest and activity
questions.explanation: This teaching, in Sahih al-Bukhari, balances worship with the rights of the body.

questions.question: Which game situation is permissible?
options: A cash bet on the final score
A football game that stops for Maghrib
A race that mocks the slowest child
Archery aimed at animals for fun
questions.explanation: The sport itself is lawful, and stopping for swalah keeps the etiquette.

questions.question: Which value is trained when players pass and share equipment?
questions.explanation: The design lists teamwork, sharing, humility, fair play, discipline and leadership.

questions.question: A match that continues on purpose through Asr is…
options: against the etiquette of observing swalah
questions.explanation: Islamic etiquette includes observing the times of swalah during games.

questions.question: How should a boy dress for sport?
questions.answer: He covers the awrah, from the navel to the knees, in clothing suitable for safe movement.
questions.explanation: Modest dress is part of the etiquette of games.

questions.question: How should a player behave after losing?
options: Lose without anger and congratulate them
questions.explanation: Humility and fair play apply after the game as well as during it.

questions.question: Archery in this Hadith should be practised…
options: in the classroom during a test
questions.explanation: It is a skill of focus and calm, done only in a safe setting.

questions.question: When is physical fitness a means of being dearer to Allah?
questions.answer: When the strong believer uses that strength to obey Allah and help people.
questions.explanation: Strength joined with iman is what the Hadith praises, not bullying or showing off.
